messages.content: Let's finish the two road hotels for Charleston. July 11 should be Hoover outside Birmingham, and July 18 is the eastern Atlanta suburbs, not Hoover again. We need one room for the three of us.

I have the correction. The best fully priced options are: in Hoover, the Courtyard Birmingham Hoover at $184.86 total for two queen beds, or the Hampton Inn & Suites Hoover-Galleria at $203.71 total for two queens. In Conyers, east of Atlanta, La Quinta by Wyndham is $162.63 total for two queens, while Holiday Inn Express is $178.40 total. All four allow three registered guests and include overnight self-parking.
What accounts for the difference in Hoover?

The Courtyard total is $159 before tax and $184.86 after tax. Breakfast is not included, but cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. Central on July 10 and payment is collected at check-in. The Hampton is $175 before tax and $203.71 total; breakfast is included, payment is also at check-in, and its free-cancellation deadline is 11:59 p.m. Central on July 9.
For these two driving nights only, don't eliminate a good hotel just because breakfast isn't free. We may need to leave before breakfast anyway.

Then the Courtyard is the stronger Hoover choice: it saves $18.85, has the later cancellation deadline, and confirms two queen beds for two adults and one 14-year-old. The desk is staffed overnight. The reservation remains guaranteed after midnight as long as the card authorization succeeds, though calling if arrival slips past 11:00 p.m. is recommended.
Good. Now compare the Conyers terms. We would probably arrive around 9:30 that night.

La Quinta is $139 before tax and $162.63 total. It includes breakfast and parking, is payable at check-in, and can be canceled without charge until 6:00 p.m. Eastern on July 17. The Holiday Inn Express total is $178.40 with breakfast and parking, but that rate is charged now and is nonrefundable. Both have 24-hour desks and will hold a guaranteed room for a 9:30 p.m. arrival.
La Quinta is fine. Confirm there isn't a sofa-bed assumption in either room.
Confirmed. Both selected room types have two physical queen beds. Neither depends on a sofa bed, rollaway, or shared single-bed arrangement, and both reservations can list all three guests.
What will the two nights cost together, and how does that affect the $650 road allowance?

Courtyard Hoover is $184.86 and La Quinta Conyers is $162.63, so the two hotel nights total $347.49 including mandatory taxes. That leaves $302.51 of the $650 road allowance for fuel and contingency. Meals remain outside that allowance. The broader vacation estimate stays $3,181.36 because it already carried the full $650 road allowance; within it, $347.49 is now a confirmed hotel amount rather than an unpriced placeholder.
And the amount for the beach hotel and Charleston transportation is still separate within that total, correct?

Correct. The established $2,531.36 covers Hotel Folly lodging, its parking, breakfast planning, and Charleston-area transportation. Adding the $650 driving allowance produces $3,181.36. Of the driving allowance, $347.49 is assigned to these two rooms and $302.51 remains for fuel and contingency.
Book both. Use the card only to guarantee them if payment is due at the hotel, and add our estimated arrival times: about 10:30 p.m. in Hoover and 9:30 p.m. in Conyers.

Both rooms are reserved for two adults and one teenager. Courtyard Birmingham Hoover is confirmed for July 11 at $184.86 total, with two queen beds, free overnight parking, payment at check-in, free cancellation through 6:00 p.m. Central on July 10, and a 10:30 p.m. arrival note. La Quinta by Wyndham Atlanta Conyers is confirmed for July 18 at $162.63 total, with two queen beds, breakfast and parking included, payment at check-in, free cancellation through 6:00 p.m. Eastern on July 17, and a 9:30 p.m. arrival note. The card was used only as a guarantee; no room charge was collected now. Together they cost $347.49, leaving $302.51 in the road allowance.
